questions.question_text:
A seed bank stores $329$ packets of vegetable seeds and $184$ packets of flower seeds.
How many packets are stored altogether?

options.why: The ones-column carry was omitted when adding the tens.
The $8$ tens in $184$ were misread as $6$ tens before adding.
The two quantities were subtracted instead of combined.

questions.question_text:
A theatre printed $940$ tickets and sold $365$.
How many tickets were not sold?

options.why: The tens column was not reduced after lending one ten to the ones.
The hundreds column was not reduced after regrouping one hundred.
Each pair of digits was subtracted larger minus smaller without regrouping.

questions.question_text:
A coastal track is $834$ m long and a forest track is $597$ m long.
How much longer is the coastal track?

options.why: After using $600$, the adjustment of $3$ was subtracted instead of added back.
The $5$ hundreds in $597$ were treated as $4$ hundreds.
Each column used the larger digit minus the smaller digit without regrouping.

questions.question_text:
A choir has learnt $462$ lines of a $700$-line performance.
How many lines remain to be learnt?

options.why: The known amount was added to the target instead of finding the gap.
The $6$ tens in $462$ were treated as $5$ tens when subtracting.
The $2$ ones were added instead of subtracted: $700-400-60+2=242$.

questions.question_text:
Three classes donated $175$, $208$ and $147$ pencils.
How many pencils did they donate altogether?

options.why: The carry of $2$ tens from the ones-column total of $20$ was omitted.
The carry into the hundreds column was omitted after adding the tens.
Only the first two class totals were added; the third was left out.

questions.question_text:
A hall had $1250$ chairs.
Staff brought in $386$ more and removed $429$.
How many chairs were then in the hall?

options.why: Only the first step was completed, so the removed chairs were not subtracted.
The removal was subtracted from the starting amount and the delivery was ignored.
Both changes were added, so the removed chairs increased the total.

questions.question_text:
Jan has £43, earns £15 doing chores, and spends £24 on a new T-shirt.
How much money does Jan have left?

options.why: Subtracts the expenditure from the initial money and ignores the earnings.
Adds the earnings and initial money but fails to subtract the purchase.
Adds all three amounts instead of treating the T-shirt as spending.

questions.solution_text: Jan has $£43+£15=£58$ before buying the T-shirt. After spending £24, the balance is $£58-£24=£34$.

questions.question_text:
Sanjay bought a new TV and laptop.
The total cost is £2200.
The laptop cost £950.
How much did the TV cost?

options.why: Adds the laptop cost to the total rather than subtracting it to find the missing cost.
Subtracts £900 but then adds £50, treating subtraction of £950 as subtraction of £900 plus £50.
Treats £950 as £1050 when subtracting from £2200, an error in regrouping around £1000.

questions.solution_text:
Subtract the laptop cost from the total cost:
$£2200-£950=£1250$.
The TV cost £1250.
